required_fixes.current: Tax on the payout. Vacation compensation is ordinary taxable employment income within the monthly withholding base. It also enters the social-security contribution base and the payroll-levy base, because vacation is paid rest, not a statutory benefit — a point frequently missed on termination settlements.
required_fixes.proposed: Tax on the payout. Vacation compensation is ordinary taxable employment income within the monthly withholding base. It is not salary, so it does not enter the health, pension and occupational-risk contribution base (Consejo de Estado, Sección Cuarta, exp. 26941 of 4 April 2024; unification ruling exp. 25185 of 9 December 2021, rule 1); it does enter the payroll-levy base for the family compensation fund, SENA and ICBF, because Law 21 of 1982 art. 17 covers paid rest whether taken or paid in cash (Law 89 of 1988 art. 1 par. 1; Consejo de Estado, Sala de Consulta, concept 2027 of 4 October 2010) — a point frequently missed on termination settlements.

required_fixes.current: Open item — high-risk pension activities. Decree-Law 2090 of 2003 establishes the high-risk activities that carry an additional employer pension contribution and a reduced retirement age, and the electronic payroll XML carries a required AltoRiesgoPension flag. The contribution-return rate table of Resolution 2388 of 2016 shows a total pension rate of 26% for a high-risk contributor (against the standard 16%), implying an additional 10 percentage points borne by the employer. CONFIRMED: the additional employer contribution is stated in the primary source. Decreto-Ley 2090 de 2003 art. 5: 'El monto de la cotización especial para las actividades de alto riesgo es el previsto en la Ley 100 de 1993, más diez (10) puntos adicionales a cargo del empleador'. So 26% total pension (16% standard + 10 points, employer-borne) is the 2026 rate. Regime validity: art. 8, as extended by Decreto 2655 de 2014, limited the special regime to workers in those activities up to 31 December 2024; workers already affiliated stay covered (art. 8 inc. 3). MinTrabajo Resolución 6072 de 2024 gave operating instructions. Decreto 1435 of 24 December 2025 (D.O. 26-12-2025) extended the regime 'hasta cuando el Congreso de la República expida la ley correspondiente', and it covers workers in those activities 'con independencia de la fecha de su vinculación laboral'. Still open: how the 10 points apply to workers who started a high-risk activity between 1 January 2025 and the decree's publication (no rule found). Configure the 10 points; re-check if Congress legislates (the decree requires a bill within 12 months).

required_fixes.current: The 13-minimum-wage floor and the 70%-then-ceiling sequence, extended. Labour Code art. 132 num. 2 (as substituted by Law 50 de 1990 art. 18) sets the minimum all-inclusive salary at 10 minimum wages of ordinary salary PLUS a factor of not less than 30% of that amount -- 13 minimum wages in total, COP 22,761,765 for 2026. Below 13 minimum wages the integral-salary stipulation does not meet art. 132 num. 2, so it cannot validly absorb statutory benefits, surcharges and premiums. The worked example above never tests the 25-minimum-wage ceiling because 70% of COP 25,000,000 (17,500,000) sits well below it. The sequence matters, so it is worth making explicit with a number that actually binds: for the SAME executive on an all-inclusive salary of COP 70,000,000, 70% is 49,000,000 -- ABOVE the 25-minimum-wage ceiling of 43,772,625. The 70% factor is applied FIRST, to the full all-inclusive salary; the ceiling is then tested against THAT result, not against some pre-adjusted figure -- so the contribution and payroll-levy base for this employee is capped at 43,772,625, not at 70% of some ceiling-adjusted salary. The withholding-tax and vacation-accrual treatment do not change: both still run on the full COP 70,000,000, exactly as in steps 4 to 6 above, since the ceiling is a social-security-contribution rule only. CONFIRMED AGAIN 19 September 2026, directly from the statute's own sequence: Ley 100 de 1993 art. 18, as rewritten by Ley 797 de 2003 art. 5, states the rules in this order within the SAME article -- (i) the base is the monthly salary, (ii) "el limite de la base de cotizacion sera de 25 salarios minimos", THEN, as the article's next and final substantive rule, (iii) "las cotizaciones de los trabajadores cuya remuneracion se pacte bajo la modalidad de salario integral, se calculara sobre el 70% de dicho salario." Rule (iii) computes what "la base de cotizacion" IS for an integral-salary worker; that resulting figure is then the thing tested against the ceiling already stated in rule (ii) -- the statute never gives a separate, pre-adjusted ceiling for salario integral. This is not merely UGPP's reading; it follows from the order the amending article itself uses. Ley 2381 de 2024 art. 22 restates the same 25-minimum-wage ceiling and the same 70% rule.
